item.title: China-linked critical minerals price swings delay 1 in 4 energy-storage projects: report
item.description: Price volatility in critical minerals, largely shaped by China’s market, is delaying or derailing nearly one in four energy-storage investments worldwide, according to a new report, highlighting the extent to which strategic materials have become a growing geopolitical flashpoint. Some 23 per cent of investors, lenders, developers and producers said otherwise viable energy-storage projects had been deferred or scrapped because of unpredictable pricing, said a report published by law firm DLA...

item.title: In US or China, firms need AI they can independently verify and trust
item.description: When the Magnificent Seven, America’s top tech companies, shed more than US$1 trillion in a single trading session, the usual question returned: is artificial intelligence (AI) a bubble? Yet as global headlines are transfixed by the personal and governance crises shaking Silicon Valley’s titan icons, that debate is already stale. Separate technology from stock prices and a harder truth emerges: multitrillion-dollar empires cannot merely survive on founder mythology and self-policing. The public...

item.title: US citizen, ‘Chinese blood’: top biologist Yuan Junying caught in debate over returnees
item.description: A top Chinese-American biologist who left Harvard University to take up a position in China is facing an online backlash amid a growing debate over whether senior returnees are squeezing out the country’s young scientists. Yuan Junying, a pioneer in the study of how cells die, drew attention in China late last month when she defended her US citizenship after winning a major science prize at the World Laureates Forum in her hometown of Shanghai. “I’ve always said my blood is Chinese blood,” said...

item.title: Hoax bomb alerts sent to schools in Italy, UK and Ireland
item.description: Schools across Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after around 6,300 of them received bomb warnings, the latest in a series of threats and cyberattacks around Europe against supermarkets, blood banks, air ‌traffic and broadcasters. Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland said many of their schools also received a similar email threat from abroad, but it was quickly classed as a hoax and did not disrupt classes. item.title: BYD apologises for wheel-rim error as China cracks down on car quality issues
item.description: BYD has apologised for an assembly error that caused some of its electric cars in China to be fitted with incorrect wheel rims, as Beijing ramps up scrutiny of quality issues in the country’s car industry. The world’s largest electric vehicle (EV) maker confirmed in a statement on Wednesday that a supplier had installed the front and rear wheel rims in reverse on some of its Tang model SUVs, offering free replacements to affected owners.
